--- file: tests/mutation_newsymbol.py ---
"""Row 459: does a pure-addition symbol, rather than a weak test, explain a
reverted run's failures? `mutation_check._resolve_import_chain` asks this
before keep-and-rerun, which would erase an independent failure's evidence.

Known gaps (adversarial-only): a runtime-built name (`'A' + 'B'`, `''.join`,
`eval`), a new METHOD reached only via a string `hasattr`/`getattr` beside an
unrelated module-level addition, and a non-test helper named `test*` (binned
as a test, so never in `outside`)."""
import ast
import re

RESULT_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(ERROR|FAIL): (\S+).*?\n-{5,}\n(.*?)(?=\n={5,}\n|\n-{5,}\nRan )",
    re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
)
_INSTANCE_ATTR_ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"AttributeError: '\w+' object has no attribute '(\w+)'")


def _mentions(nodes):
    names = {n.id for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
    names |= {n.attr for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute)}
    strs = [n.value for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str)]
    names |= set(strs) | {p for v in strs for p in v.split(".")}  # 'mod.X' patch targets
    return names


def collect(test_src, support_srcs):
    """`(referenced_by_test, outside)`: what each `test*` function mentions, and
    what everything else mentions - the rest of the test file plus each changed
    test-support file (never reverted, so it may still name the symbol)."""
    test_tree = ast.parse(test_src or "")
    referenced_by_test, skip = {}, set()
    for node in ast.walk(test_tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name.startswith("test"):
            sub = list(ast.walk(node))
            skip.update(id(n) for n in sub)
            referenced_by_test.setdefault(node.name, set()).update(_mentions(sub))
    outside = _mentions([n for n in ast.walk(test_tree) if id(n) not in skip])
    for src in support_srcs:
        try:
            outside |= _mentions(list(ast.walk(ast.parse(src or ""))))
        except SyntaxError:  # an unparseable module cannot be imported, so it mentions nothing
            continue
    return referenced_by_test, outside


def addition_explains_failures(out, known_symbols, context, symbol_res):
    """Each result block names a `known_symbols` name (`saw_known`, matched by
    `symbol_res` or an instance AttributeError) or names nothing AND neither
    its test nor `outside` references one (`saw_other`). An unknown symbol
    aborts outright. Needs both."""
    referenced_by_test, outside = context
    saw_known = saw_other = False
    for m in RESULT_BLOCK_RE.finditer(out or ""):
        test_name, body = m.group(2), m.group(3)
        sm = next(filter(None, (r.search(body) for r in (*symbol_res, _INSTANCE_ATTR_ERROR_RE))), None)
        if sm:
            if sm.group(sm.lastindex) not in known_symbols:
                return False
            saw_known = True
        elif not ((referenced_by_test.get(test_name, set()) | outside) & known_symbols):
            saw_other = True
    return saw_known and saw_other

"""Row 459: does a pure-addition symbol, rather than a weak test, explain a
reverted run's failures? `mutation_check._resolve_import_chain` asks this
before keep-and-rerun, which would erase an independent failure's evidence.

Known gaps (adversarial-only): a runtime-built name (`'A' + 'B'`, `''.join`,
`eval`), a new METHOD reached only via a string `hasattr`/`getattr` beside an
unrelated module-level addition, and a non-test helper named `test*` (binned
as a test, so never in `outside`)."""
import ast
import re

# Card t_a7491776: a pure-addition module can add MORE than one brand-new top-level
# name at once (`paths.resolve_config` plus a second addition, the real repro). The
# import/attribute error that triggers a keep only ever names ONE of them - seeding
# `known_symbols` with just that one name left every OTHER addition's own result block
# reading as an "unknown symbol" to `addition_explains_failures`, which aborts outright
# on the very first one it sees - even with a genuinely independent failure elsewhere in
# the same run, the whole module then falls through to keep-and-rerun, which SUCCEEDS
# (every addition is restored) and reads as a plain pass - "did not fail (BAD)" for a
# file that was, in fact, discriminating. `known_names` seeds the full set instead: once
# a module is judged a pure addition and about to be kept in full, every name IT adds is
# equally "explained", not just the one the regex happened to match.
_TOP_LEVEL_TARGET_TYPES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)


def _add_target(node, names):
    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
        names.add(node.id)
    elif isinstance(node, (ast.Tuple, ast.List)):
        for elt in node.elts:
            _add_target(elt, names)


def _added_top_level_names(base_source, head_source):
    """Top-level names (`def`/`class`, simple or unpacking assignment, or a top-level
    `import`/`from ... import` binding) HEAD's module defines that base's version does
    not - a lighter-weight duplicate of `mutation_check._top_level_names`, kept here
    rather than imported: `mutation_check` imports this module at collection time, so
    importing back would cycle."""
    def names(source):
        try:
            tree = ast.parse(source or "")
        except SyntaxError:
            return set()
        out = set()
        for node in tree.body:
            if isinstance(node, _TOP_LEVEL_TARGET_TYPES):
                out.add(node.name)
            elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
                for t in node.targets:
                    _add_target(t, out)
            elif isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign):
                _add_target(node.target, out)
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                out |= {a.asname or a.name for a in node.names}
            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                out |= {a.asname or a.name.split(".")[0] for a in node.names}
        return out
    return names(head_source) - names(base_source)


def known_names(kept, symbol, base_source, head_source):
    """`known_symbols` for the CURRENT module being judged: every symbol already kept
    for an earlier module in this chain, `symbol` itself (the one the regex matched),
    and every OTHER brand-new top-level name this module's own base/head diff adds -
    all equally "explained" once the whole module is restored."""
    return {s for _, s in kept} | {symbol} | _added_top_level_names(base_source, head_source)

RESULT_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(ERROR|FAIL): (\S+).*?\n-{5,}\n(.*?)(?=\n={5,}\n|\n-{5,}\nRan )",
    re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL,
)
_INSTANCE_ATTR_ERROR_RE = re.compile(r"AttributeError: '\w+' object has no attribute '(\w+)'")


def _mentions(nodes):
    names = {n.id for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
    names |= {n.attr for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute)}
    strs = [n.value for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str)]
    names |= set(strs) | {p for v in strs for p in v.split(".")}  # 'mod.X' patch targets
    return names


def collect(test_src, support_srcs):
    """`(referenced_by_test, outside)`: what each `test*` function mentions, and
    what everything else mentions - the rest of the test file plus each changed
    test-support file (never reverted, so it may still name the symbol)."""
    test_tree = ast.parse(test_src or "")
    referenced_by_test, skip = {}, set()
    for node in ast.walk(test_tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name.startswith("test"):
            sub = list(ast.walk(node))
            skip.update(id(n) for n in sub)
            referenced_by_test.setdefault(node.name, set()).update(_mentions(sub))
    outside = _mentions([n for n in ast.walk(test_tree) if id(n) not in skip])
    for src in support_srcs:
        try:
            outside |= _mentions(list(ast.walk(ast.parse(src or ""))))
        except SyntaxError:  # an unparseable module cannot be imported, so it mentions nothing
            continue
    return referenced_by_test, outside


def addition_explains_failures(out, known_symbols, context, symbol_res):
    """Each result block names a `known_symbols` name (`saw_known`, matched by
    `symbol_res` or an instance AttributeError) or names nothing AND neither
    its test nor `outside` references one (`saw_other`). An unknown symbol
    aborts outright. Needs both."""
    referenced_by_test, outside = context
    saw_known = saw_other = False
    for m in RESULT_BLOCK_RE.finditer(out or ""):
        test_name, body = m.group(2), m.group(3)
        sm = next(filter(None, (r.search(body) for r in (*symbol_res, _INSTANCE_ATTR_ERROR_RE))), None)
        if sm:
            if sm.group(sm.lastindex) not in known_symbols:
                return False
            saw_known = True
        elif not ((referenced_by_test.get(test_name, set()) | outside) & known_symbols):
            saw_other = True
    return saw_known and saw_other
--- file: tests/mutation_check.py ---
import mutation_newsymbol as newsymbol


def _resolve_import_chain(repo, base, head, wt, test_path, prod_files, names, weaken_is_good=False):
    """Keep-and-rerun `test_path`'s `names` selection inside worktree `wt`
    until collection stops failing on a resolvable missing-new-name shape, a
    genuinely different failure surfaces, `CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT` modules
    have been kept without resolving, or the exact same `(module, symbol)`
    resolution repeats (a cycle, review round 1 finding 6 - no point burning
    the remaining iterations' timeouts, each at least 180s, on a repeat).

    Handles a collection-time `cannot import name 'X' from 'M'` AND (card
    t_285a8851) a run-time `AttributeError: module 'M' has no attribute 'X'`
    inside a test body, which `is_collection_error` never sees - so it is
    tried before the collection-error branch, not instead of it.

    Returns `(state, extra, out, kept)`:
      - state="resolved": `extra` is the final `rc`, `out` the final output,
        `kept` the (possibly empty) list of `(module_path, symbol)` restored.
        A genuine pass/fail (or an unrelated failure that reached test
        execution) is scored normally by the caller from `extra`/`kept`.
      - state="napt": the resolvable module's diff is not additions-only AND
        no module has been kept yet (`kept` is empty); `extra` is the symbol
        name (n/a, weaken carries the requirement) - unchanged from round 10.
      - state="addition_explained" (row 459, only when `weaken_is_good`): the
        pure additions explain every failure; `extra` names them, no keep.
      - state="new_module": the collection error is explained by a production
        file that is new in this range (round 2's rule); `extra` is None.
      - state="error": a genuinely unrelated/broken collection error
        (`extra` is None); the review round 1 fail-closed backstop
        (`extra` is None); OR a napt hit found PARTWAY down an already
        non-empty chain (review round 1 finding 5 - reaching n/a directly
        here would be a quieter version of round 10's plain ERROR for the
        exact same shape; `extra` is the `(module_path, symbol)` that wasn't
        a pure addition, `kept` still carries every module resolved before
        it, so the caller's label shows the whole chain).
      - state="unresolved": `CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT` modules were kept, or the
        same `(module_path, symbol)` resolution repeated, and it still
        doesn't resolve; `extra` is the `(module_path, symbol)` that could
        not be kept (the Nth name, review round 1 finding 6), `kept` names
        every module/symbol actually resolved before it.

    Every module written into `wt` to "keep" it is restored back to its
    `--base` content before this function returns, on every exit path - the
    caller sees `wt` exactly as it found it, just like `make_worktree`/
    `remove_worktree` bracket the whole revert phase."""
    kept = []
    seen = set()
    new_prod_files = [pf for pf in prod_files if file_status(repo, base, head, pf) == "A"]
    context = newsymbol.collect(show_file(repo, head, test_path), [
        show_file(repo, head, f) for f in changed_files(repo, base, head) if is_test_support_file(f)])
    try:
        while True:
            rc, out = run_discover(wt, (wt / test_path).parent, Path(test_path).name, names)
            if rc == 0:
                return "resolved", rc, out, list(kept)
            symbol_hit = analyze_symbol_import_error(out, repo, base, head, prod_files)
            if symbol_hit is not None:
                module_path, symbol, additions_only = symbol_hit
                if not additions_only:
                    return (("error", (module_path, symbol)) if kept else ("napt", symbol)) + (out, list(kept))
                known = newsymbol.known_names(kept, symbol, show_file(repo, base, module_path), show_file(repo, head, module_path))
                if weaken_is_good and not is_collection_error(out) and newsymbol.addition_explains_failures(
                        out, known, context, (CANNOT_IMPORT_RE, ATTRIBUTE_ERROR_RE)):
                    return "addition_explained", ", ".join(sorted(known)), out, list(kept)
                if (module_path, symbol) in seen or len(kept) >= CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT:
                    return "unresolved", (module_path, symbol), out, list(kept)
                (wt / module_path).write_text(show_file(repo, head, module_path), encoding="utf-8")
                kept.append((module_path, symbol))
                seen.add((module_path, symbol))
                continue
            if is_collection_error(out):
                if new_module_import_error(out, new_prod_files):
                    return "new_module", None, out, list(kept)
                return "error", None, out, list(kept)
            if _mentions_missing_prod_symbol(out, repo, base, prod_files):
                return "error", None, out, list(kept)
            # rc != 0, not a resolvable missing-new-name shape, not a
            # collection error at all: a genuine failure (or a genuinely
            # unrelated run-time error) that reached test execution.
            return "resolved", rc, out, list(kept)
    finally:
        for module_path, _ in kept:
            revert_to_base(repo, base, wt, module_path, file_status(repo, base, head, module_path))

import mutation_newsymbol as newsymbol


def _resolve_import_chain(repo, base, head, wt, test_path, prod_files, names, weaken_is_good=False):
    """Keep-and-rerun `test_path`'s `names` selection inside worktree `wt`
    until collection stops failing on a resolvable missing-new-name shape, a
    genuinely different failure surfaces, `CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT` modules
    have been kept without resolving, or the exact same `(module, symbol)`
    resolution repeats (a cycle, review round 1 finding 6 - no point burning
    the remaining iterations' timeouts, each at least 180s, on a repeat).

    Handles a collection-time `cannot import name 'X' from 'M'` AND (card
    t_285a8851) a run-time `AttributeError: module 'M' has no attribute 'X'`
    inside a test body, which `is_collection_error` never sees - so it is
    tried before the collection-error branch, not instead of it.

    Returns `(state, extra, out, kept)`:
      - state="resolved": `extra` is the final `rc`, `out` the final output,
        `kept` the (possibly empty) list of `(module_path, symbol)` restored.
        A genuine pass/fail (or an unrelated failure that reached test
        execution) is scored normally by the caller from `extra`/`kept`.
      - state="napt": the resolvable module's diff is not additions-only AND
        no module has been kept yet (`kept` is empty); `extra` is the symbol
        name (n/a, weaken carries the requirement) - unchanged from round 10.
      - state="addition_explained" (row 459, only when `weaken_is_good`): the
        pure additions explain every failure; `extra` names them, no keep.
      - state="new_module": the collection error is explained by a production
        file that is new in this range (round 2's rule); `extra` is None.
      - state="error": a genuinely unrelated/broken collection error
        (`extra` is None); the review round 1 fail-closed backstop
        (`extra` is None); OR a napt hit found PARTWAY down an already
        non-empty chain (review round 1 finding 5 - reaching n/a directly
        here would be a quieter version of round 10's plain ERROR for the
        exact same shape; `extra` is the `(module_path, symbol)` that wasn't
        a pure addition, `kept` still carries every module resolved before
        it, so the caller's label shows the whole chain).
      - state="unresolved": `CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT` modules were kept, or the
        same `(module_path, symbol)` resolution repeated, and it still
        doesn't resolve; `extra` is the `(module_path, symbol)` that could
        not be kept (the Nth name, review round 1 finding 6), `kept` names
        every module/symbol actually resolved before it.

    Every module written into `wt` to "keep" it is restored back to its
    `--base` content before this function returns, on every exit path - the
    caller sees `wt` exactly as it found it, just like `make_worktree`/
    `remove_worktree` bracket the whole revert phase."""
    kept = []
    seen = set()
    new_prod_files = [pf for pf in prod_files if file_status(repo, base, head, pf) == "A"]
    context = newsymbol.collect(show_file(repo, head, test_path), [
        show_file(repo, head, f) for f in changed_files(repo, base, head) if is_test_support_file(f)])
    try:
        while True:
            rc, out = run_discover(wt, (wt / test_path).parent, Path(test_path).name, names)
            if rc == 0:
                return "resolved", rc, out, list(kept)
            symbol_hit = analyze_symbol_import_error(out, repo, base, head, prod_files)
            if symbol_hit is not None:
                module_path, symbol, additions_only = symbol_hit
                if not additions_only:
                    return (("error", (module_path, symbol)) if kept else ("napt", symbol)) + (out, list(kept))
                known = newsymbol.known_names(kept, symbol, show_file(repo, base, module_path), show_file(repo, head, module_path))
                if weaken_is_good and not is_collection_error(out) and newsymbol.addition_explains_failures(
                        out, known, context, (CANNOT_IMPORT_RE, ATTRIBUTE_ERROR_RE)):
                    return "addition_explained", ", ".join(sorted(known)), out, list(kept)
                if (module_path, symbol) in seen or len(kept) >= CHAIN_ITERATION_LIMIT:
                    return "unresolved", (module_path, symbol), out, list(kept)
                (wt / module_path).write_text(show_file(repo, head, module_path), encoding="utf-8")
                kept.append((module_path, symbol))
                seen.add((module_path, symbol))
                continue
            if is_collection_error(out):
                if new_module_import_error(out, new_prod_files):
                    return "new_module", None, out, list(kept)
                return "error", None, out, list(kept)
            if _mentions_missing_prod_symbol(out, repo, base, prod_files):
                return "error", None, out, list(kept)
            # rc != 0, not a resolvable missing-new-name shape, not a
            # collection error at all: a genuine failure (or a genuinely
            # unrelated run-time error) that reached test execution.
            return "resolved", rc, out, list(kept)
    finally:
        for module_path, _ in kept:
            revert_to_base(repo, base, wt, module_path, file_status(repo, base, head, module_path))
